deliverables.title: Current-state architecture map
deliverables.description: A diagram and written model of the system as it is today, not as it was designed. Derived from the running code and confirmed with the people who operate it.

deliverables.title: System inventory
deliverables.description: Every deployed service, datastore, scheduled job, and third-party dependency, with owner and criticality. The list nobody has in one place.

deliverables.title: Operator interviews
deliverables.description: Notes from the people who run the system day to day. The problems worth solving are usually named here and nowhere in the codebase.

deliverables.title: Functional requirements
deliverables.description: What the system must do, stated so that a disagreement about scope can be settled by reading it.

deliverables.title: Non-functional requirements
deliverables.description: Latency, availability, throughput, retention, residency, and cost ceilings — each with a number and the source of that number.

deliverables.title: Risk register
deliverables.description: Each risk with likelihood, impact, owner, and the trigger that would tell us it is happening. A risk with no owner is a wish.

deliverables.title: Dependency register
deliverables.description: Upstream and downstream dependencies including the human ones — teams, vendors, and approvals that gate delivery.

deliverables.title: Technical-debt register
deliverables.description: Debt itemised with the interest it charges: what it costs per change, not just that it exists.

deliverables.title: Prioritized roadmap with effort and sequencing
deliverables.description: Ordered work with effort estimates and the dependencies that force the order. The output the engagement is actually judged on.

deliverables.title: Agreed success criteria
deliverables.description: The criteria the pilot will be judged against, recorded as gates before the pilot starts. Criteria written afterwards measure nothing.

deliverables.title: Working pilot deployed in your environment
deliverables.description: Running on the client's infrastructure, against the client's data. A pilot on our laptop proves our laptop works.

gates.title: Inventory is complete
gates.criterion: Every deployed system, datastore, and scheduled job appears in the inventory with a named owner.
gates.measurement: Reconcile the inventory against the cloud account, the CI project list, and the on-call rotation. Any system in one and not the other is a miss.

gates.title: Requirements are testable
gates.criterion: Every non-functional requirement carries a number and the source of that number.
gates.measurement: Read each NFR and attempt to write the assertion that would falsify it. An NFR that cannot be falsified is not a requirement.

gates.title: Roadmap is sequenced by dependency
gates.criterion: Every roadmap item's position is explained by a dependency, a risk, or a stated business date — not by preference.
gates.measurement: Walk the roadmap and name the constraint fixing each item's position. Unexplained ordering fails.

gates.title: Criteria agreed before the pilot ran
gates.criterion: The success criteria were recorded and accepted before the pilot began.
gates.measurement: Compare each gate's creation timestamp against the pilot's start. A criterion created after the start is evidence of the outcome, not a test of it.

gates.title: Pilot ran on client infrastructure and client data
gates.criterion: The pilot executed in the client's environment against the client's data, not a synthetic sample.
gates.measurement: Deployment target and dataset provenance recorded as evidence on the pilot deliverable.
